stories.title: US to hold off on Iran attack in hope of deal - Trump
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has said that he would hold off on a fresh attack on Iran as long as a deal could be reached quickly to halt Iran's nuclear ambitions and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran and "other Middle Eastern Countries" asked for a time to complete a deal that would lead to "the Immediate, Complete and Total" reopening of the Strait and "an end to Iran's nuclear threat," Mr Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. "Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL." Israel "joins me in this commitment," he wrote. Israel did not immediately make a public statement on the issue.

stories.title: High Court finds Tusla in contempt of court
stories.summary: The High Court has found the Child and Family Agency Tusla is in contempt of court for failing to provide secure placements for vulnerable children despite being directed to do so. Legal sources say it is believed to be the first time a State agency has been held to be in contempt of court. The action was taken on behalf of three children in respect of whom special care orders were made by the High Court. Ms Justice Emily Egan said even though these children had now received placements, it was a systemic and recurring problem and there were still five to seven children every week for whom no special care beds were available despite orders being made.

stories.summary: The UK's ruling Labour Party comfortably retained the mayoralty of Greater Manchester following an election triggered by new Prime Minister Andy Burnham's return to parliament. Bev Craig, the leader of Manchester City Council, was elected after winning 47.15% of the votes in the first round. The anti-immigration Reform UK party, which had been riding high in national polls, came in second place with a 21% share. Without the 50% of votes needed to win outright, the counting proceeded to a second round.

stories.summary: Bank of Ireland has reported a 33% jump in pre-tax profits for the six months to the end of June and said it was upgrading its guidance for the full year. Bank of Ireland said its half year pre-tax profits rose to €960m, and it also announced an interim dividend of 39 cent per share, an increase of 56%. Lending during the six month period rose by 4% to €84 billion. Bank of Ireland noted an "excellent" performance in its Irish lending which rose by €2.2 billion - up 7% - but it saw a fall of €0.5 billion in its UK lending where it said it prioritised value over volume.

stories.summary: Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja is among those who have died after a powerful avalanche on one of the world's highest peaks, his climbing company has confirmed. The 43-year-old was one of ten climbers missing following the avalanche in Pakistan. The British-Nepali mountaineer was leading an expedition of the climbers on Broad Peak - the world's 12th highest mountain - in the north of the country when the avalanche struck on Thursday. Following search efforts which resumed this morning, his company Elite Exped confirmed that Mr Purja was killed.

stories.summary: Pierce O'Leary has suffered a 10th-round knock-out defeat in his IBO World super lightweight championship title defence against England's Mark Chamberlain at the 3Arena in Dublin. Chamberlain, who pulled out of a scheduled showdown between the pair in March due to a chest infection, caught previously unbeaten O'Leary on the ropes with a numbing combination before the referee stepped in to stop the fight. The 27-year-old Englishman silenced O’Leary’s fans as the Dubliner crashed to his first professional defeat. O’Leary, bidding for a 20th straight professional win, was floored by a left to the nose in the second round and again by another left in the third before recovering his composure to take the fight to his opponent.

Captain Síofra O'Shea racked up 1-08 as Kerry comprehensively dispatched the reigning champions Dublin in the Thurles semi-final, winning 2-16 to 1-09 in the finish and they enter the finale as clear favourites. The westerners, who claimed another Connacht title earlier this year, easily accounted for Armagh in the other semi.

stories.title: Sligo strike late to snatch priceless point at Dundalk
stories.summary: Gareth McElroy scored what could be a huge stoppage time goal as Sligo Rovers rescued a late point against Dundalk at Oriel Park. Ciarán Kilduff's side looked to be cruising towards victory when captain Daryl Horgan fired them ahead early in the second half with what was the 100th goal of his club career. However, despite dominating proceedings the Louth men failed to find the crucial second, with Sligo – who conceded late against Drogheda Utd six days earlier – punishing a late error to make it two points from as many matches for new boss Darren Purse. While the Bit O' Red remain bottom of the table on goal difference, this result will give them a huge boost ahead of next week’s trip to face Derry City.

stories.title: Buffalo Traffic Jam: best pals, one of 2026's best albums
stories.summary: As life 180s go, things have worked out brilliantly for Buffalo Traffic Jam's Frankie Cassidy and Nathan Ross. Right about now, the 2025 graduates in architecture (Cassidy) and mechanical engineering (Ross) should be climbing the first rungs on the corporate ladder. "We didn't play our first gig together until 2024 at a local Montana venue called The Filling Station," smiles Cassidy as he bashfully tries to get his head around the past two years. "That was our first time we ever played live."

stories.title: Met Gala 2027 will honour controversial designer John Galliano
stories.summary: The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced that its next exhibition will celebrate the career of John Galliano, whose renowned stint as the Creative Director at Dior ended after he was filmed making antisemitic and racist remarks outside a Paris cafe in 2011. John Galliano: Horizons will be on display at The Met from May 9, 2027 until January 9, 2028, and will be a career-spanning look at a figure largely regarded by the fashion industry as one of the most influential designers of the last number of decades. The exhibition will be kicked off by the annual Met Gala on 3 May, where the A-list attendees will be sure to pay homage to Galliano's work. With this exhibit, Galliano becomes only the third living designer to have their work featured in a solo exhibition by the institute, after Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo of Comme des Garçons in 2017.

stories.title: Three killed after bomb attack near Moscow restaurant
stories.summary: A homemade bomb carried by a woman killed three people and injured at least 21 in an explosion near an upscale restaurant in central Moscow yesterday evening, according to authorities. The explosion occurred just before 8pm local time close to an Italian restaurant located in one of Moscow's seven Stalin-era skyscrapers at Kudrinkskaya Square, the police said. Russia's Anti-Terrorism Committee said that an unidentified woman had tried to get into the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard, the state RIA news agency reported. It said the woman, the security guard and a customer at the Balzi Rossi Italian restaurant had been killed in the blast that followed.

stories.summary: Fleadh Cheoil na hÉireann will get under way in Belfast for the first time in the event's history this afternoon. Earlier this month Aer Lingus said that up to 500 jobs could be cut at the airline due to a planned 6% reduction in its flight capacity. Under the cost-cutting plan, 290 roles are under threat in head office functions, along with 140 cabin roles and 70 pilot positions. Aer Lingus said today that its costs increased by 8% in the first half of the year and passenger revenue decreased by 3%.

stories.title: US drops vandalism charge against former Olympian
stories.summary: The US Justice Department has dropped its case against a former Olympian accused of damaging the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, saying the hurried renovations ordered by President Donald Trump had been botched. David Hearn, 67, had been charged with felony vandalism in federal court, which carried a potential sentence of ten years in jail. Federal prosecutor Jeanine Pirro had announced the charges in a high-profile press briefing earlier this month, saying witnesses had viewed Hearn "forcefully and violently" pulling up the pool's new liner on 19 June. But in a court filing yesterday, Ms Pirro said new revelations "undermine the evidentiary basis for the indictment," and moved for dismissal.

Ospreys have won the URC, in its previous guise, four times, most recently in 2012.

stories.summary: Italy said it was suspending the EU's border-free Schengen arrangements with Spain in response to a mass influx of migrants into the Spanish territory of Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco. Italy does not share a land border with Spain but the measure - which looks certain to anger Madrid - will impact people travelling by plane or boat between the two countries, meaning they will need to show a passport to gain access. The Schengen Area allows passport-free travel across 29 European countries, although member states can temporarily reintroduce border controls on security or public-order grounds. Italy's interior ministry said in a statement it had also agreed with Paris to strengthen controls along the Franco-Italian land border to try to prevent any undocumented migrants from crossing.

stories.title: Arteta promises to splash the cash to help title defence
stories.summary: Arsenal will splash more cash before the summer transfer window closes, manager Mikel Arteta said, insisting the Premier League champions will not "sit ⁠still" while they prepare to defend their first English top-flight title in 22 years. Arsenal - who play Real Betis at Aviva Stadium in Dublin on Wednesday - have been relatively quiet in the market compared to big-spending rivals Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester City and Chelsea, but the north London side have been linked with moves for Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes and Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr. While Arteta would not be ‌drawn on Arsenal's reported ⁠pursuit of the pair, he told reporters on Saturday that the club were determined to "improve and evolve" the squad. "We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously," the Spaniard added, speaking after a 4-1 pre-season win ‌over Girona.
